messages:
maria: FYI ran the CIS container baseline scan against the staging base image this morning. A handful of failures that affect runtime attack surface and signing workflow.

jake: can you paste the top failures? interested in the signer/keystore bits.

maria: main ones: 1) /tmp world-writable layers  2) old libssl version flagged (low/fixable) 3) missing cosign signature metadata in staging repo 4) auditd not forwarding container lifecycle events to our audit-shipper.

eric: for cosign, do we have a KMS integration gap or is it just missing signing during bake?

maria: looks like signing step skipped in the pipeline for this image — the keystore role used by CI doesn't have the kms:Sign binding post-rotation. RBAC change last week may have stripped it.

sophia: ugh ok. who changed the role? @kevin?

kevin: that was me — I tightened the role to remove broad Sign permissions for the builder principal. I thought the builder would use a separate signer service but apparently not. we can add a scoped kms:Sign for the cosign key only.

jake: approve scoped fix. we should also update the pipeline to fail if signature missing. quick patch: check for signature file after bake and fail early.

maria:+1. I sketched a small check that runs in the bake job: 

```
# verify in bake step
cosign verify --key k8s://projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/cosign-key $IMAGE_URI
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "image not signed"; exit 1
fi
```

eric: also need a migration plan for already-pushed images. do we re-sign and repush or build new images?

sophia: for compliance we should rebuild with the fixed bake pipeline and repush. re-signing existing layers without rebuild will hurt provenance.

kevin: agree. I'll add the KMS role binding for the CI signer and open a short-lived PR to revert the tightened role once we have a proper signer service.

maria: other infra asks: audit logs currently only show container start/stop from kubelet, not image pull events. Security wants pull events for forensic timelines.

eric: that’s because our auditd sidecar isn't capturing containerd events by default. We can enable containerd event forwarding to auditd and ship. small config change but need canary.

sophia: can you share the config snippet?

eric: sure — add to auditd sidecar config: 

```
containerd:
  enabled: true
  events: ["pull","create","start","destroy"]
output:
  shipper: http://audit-shipper.internal/ingest
```

kevin: test it in staging first. if it floods logs we need a filter for image pull metadata only.

maria: good call. also CVE note: libssl flagged v1.1.1 -> we've got an upgrade path in baseimage distro but need rebuild runbook. this ties into the base image rebuild schedule.

jake: propose: 1) short-term: patch pipeline to require cosign verify and restore CI KMS binding, 2) enable containerd event forwarding in staging with filter, 3) schedule base image rebuilds this week to pick up libssl + remove world-writable tmp.

sophia: I'll own the rebuild runway. target window Thu 03:00-05:00 PT, canary to prod after sign-off.

kevin: I'll open PRs for the RBAC change and the bake check. tagging @maria for approval.

maria: thanks — please include a note in the PR about incident rollback plan (how to stop deploy and revoke the new key binding if something breaks).

eric: for rollback: we can disable the bake signer role and mark images as untrusted in the registry UI which will block deploys. docs snippet in the runbook: 

- steps to disable role: `gcloud iam roles remove-iam-policy-binding ...`
- registry block: mark tag as quarantined via registry API

kevin: PR link coming shortly.

attest-bot: build-scan results: staging/base-image:2026-05-07 failed 7 checks (CIS). See: https://ci.internal/scans/1758502468

maria: perfect. I'll coordinate with Sophia to set the rebuild and follow up after canary. thanks all. :thumbsup:
